tldr: This survey response page captures 30+ individual and small-business respondents addressing business climate, workforce development, housing, energy policy, and transit. Dominant themes: workforce development system fragmentation (especially early childhood and rural economies), insufficient wage standards tied to cost of living, housing shortage requiring zoning/permitting reform, public transit funding cuts, and utility wildfire liability. Respondents split between advocates for business-friendly deregulation/lower taxes and those pushing for worker-centered policies, progressive taxation (billionaire's tax models), sectoral bargaining, and increased public investment in essential services.

bullets.text: Early childhood education training shortage: respondents report only ~15% of needed workforce trained to required early learning credential standards
Portland General Electric insurance premiums increased 180% in last 5 years due to wildfire liability risk
PGE service area generates $4.6 billion in annual economic output and supports 9,421 jobs
Respondents call for union apprenticeship enrollment targets of at least 25% in key sectors (healthcare, logistics, retail, construction, hospitality)
Multiple respondents advocate preserving Multnomah County's universal preschool program as statewide model
Rural Oregon workforce advocates identify system fragmentation across K-12, higher education, workforce boards, and economic development as core barrier
Respondents cite transit funding cuts and freeway expansion (Interstate Bridge Replacement, Rose Quarter) as contradictions to economic development goals
Multiple respondents propose billionaire's tax modeled on Massachusetts and California examples
